before.title: 12V battery drains / goes flat when parked
before.description: The CX-60 has no conventional alternator; its small 12V battery (around 6.5Ah) is charged from the 48V mild-hybrid system via a DC/DC converter. Faulty Electrical Supply Unit (ESU) control software, or pressing the start button multiple times before the driver-personalisation system has recognised the driver, can prevent the car's systems from going to sleep, draining the battery within 4-8 hours of parking. Owners report needing to recharge or jump-start regularly.
before.solution: Mazda issued dealer advice / TSB R003/23 (Feb 2023) for European and UK cars and released ESU/system software updates so the vehicle properly enters sleep mode. Persistent cases may need the 12V battery replaced. Avoiding repeated start-button presses and completing driver recognition before switching off also helps.
symptoms: Flat 12V battery after parking a few hours
Car won't start / needs a jump
Battery-saving or 'drive to charge battery' warnings
Repeated need to recharge the 12V battery

before.title: AdBlue (SCR) Overfull / False Warning Messages on Diesel
before.description: Diesel CX-60 owners report AdBlue-related warnings appearing early (around 13,000 km) and, after topping up, an 'AdBlue overfull' or persistent low-AdBlue message even when the tank (~6.7 L usable) is filled correctly. If an 'overfull' or low-quality warning persists, drive ~1,000 km and re-check, then have the dealer read SCR/urea level and quality sensor data and recalibrate or replace the level sensor if it is genuinely out of range. Use only ISO 22241 (AUS 32) grade AdBlue.

before.title: Diesel DPF Frequent Regeneration and Poor Economy on Short Trips
before.description: 3.3L diesel CX-60 owners report the diesel particulate filter (DPF) entering active regeneration very often, particularly on short/urban journeys where the exhaust never reaches full temperature. During a regen the engine injects extra fuel to burn off soot, driving instantaneous consumption up to ~15-17 L/100km and dropping average economy to the mid-20s mpg. Owners who do mostly short trips risk incomplete regens, a partially clogged DPF, and eventually a limp-mode/emissions warning. Mazda advises a periodic 30-45 minute higher-speed drive to complete a regen.
before.solution: For short-trip drivers, complete an uninterrupted 30-45 minute motorway drive every 2-3 weeks to allow a full passive/active regen. If a DPF warning appears, have the dealer run a forced/service regeneration and inspect for related Denso injector spray-pattern issues. A heavily loaded DPF that will not regen may require professional cleaning or replacement.
symptoms: Frequent DPF regeneration cycles
Sudden drop in fuel economy to mid-20s mpg
Higher idle/cooling-fan running after stopping
Diesel smell after short trips
DPF or emissions warning light on short-journey use

proposal.title: Diesel DPF Frequent Regeneration and Poor Economy on Short Trips
proposal.description: Mazda explains that the diesel particulate filter captures particulate matter and periodically burns accumulated soot. proposal.solution: If the soot warning is displayed steadily and conditions are safe, follow the exact market manual: warm the engine and drive for about 15-20 minutes so regeneration can operate. A flashing warning, limited output, or a warning that does not clear requires Mazda diagnosis; do not command a forced regeneration or replace injectors, sensors or the DPF from this page. Do not buy DPF cleaner, injectors or a filter from this page; warning state, soot load, stored faults and root cause must be verified first.

before.description: The CX-60 PHEV's displayed EV range is an estimate calculated from current high-voltage-battery charge and recent energy consumption, so it can change with temperature, speed, terrain, climate-control use, and driving history and may differ from actual distance. Mazda also changes the usable lower battery boundary when the battery is cold. If usable energy or actual EV distance falls abruptly under comparable conditions, charge disappears while parked, a warning appears, or EV mode repeatedly cancels without a documented reason, ask Mazda for campaign status, high-voltage-battery state-of-health data, charging history, relevant DTCs, and BECM diagnosis. AR058A should not be cited as an EV-range recalibration campaign.

before.title: CX-60 Steering Effort Can Increase as Worm-Gear Grease Is Displaced (Recall R/2024/020 / 5430)
before.description: In affected CX-60 vehicles, the electric power-steering gearbox can have an incorrect gear-meshing load. Mazda says this can push grease away from the engagement area, increase sliding resistance, and increase the force needed to turn the steering wheel. Drivers may describe the result as sticky, notchy, or suddenly heavier steering. Recall applicability varies by VIN and market; the symptom alone does not prove that the steering rack needs replacement.
before.solution: Check the VIN with Mazda or the market's official recall service for the steering campaign. For an affected vehicle, Mazda's documented repair is to replace the worm-gear engagement spring with the countermeasure part and reapply grease to the gear engagement area. Have the authorised repairer complete and close the recall, then verify smooth steering effort and return-to-centre behavior. Do not buy a spring kit, attempt to dismantle the electric steering gear, or rely on an undocumented lock-to-lock maneuver. If symptoms remain after the recall, return for steering diagnosis rather than assuming a full rack is required.
symptoms: Sticky or notchy steering movement
Unexpected increase in steering effort
Inconsistent on-centre steering feel
Difficulty making smooth small steering corrections
affectedSystems: worm gear and worm wheel engagement
